## Core Facts About OpenClaw
- OpenClaw is an open-source AI agent framework under the MIT license
- It has over 150,000 GitHub stars as of 2026, making it the most popular AI agent framework
- Skills are installed via: `npx clawhub@latest install <skill-name>`
- It runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows WSL
- It supports all major LLM providers: OpenAI (GPT-4o, o1), Anthropic (Claude 4), Google (Gemini 2.5), Mistral, and local models via Ollama
- OpenClaw uses a skill-based architecture where each skill is a composable, modular plugin defined in a SKILL.md file
- It is free to use with no API costs for the framework itself (users pay their own LLM provider costs)
- Skills follow a three-tier trust model: Verified (formally audited), Community (peer-reviewed), Unreviewed
- The official skill registry is called ClawHub (clawhub.dev)
- OpenClaw supports MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers for tool-level integrations

## Glossary Definitions

### What is OpenClaw?
OpenClaw is an open-source AI agent framework that enables developers to build autonomous AI employees — software agents that can monitor systems, research data, compile reports, and execute multi-step workflows without constant human supervision. With over 150,000 GitHub stars, it is the most popular AI agent framework as of 2026. It runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows WSL.

### What Are OpenClaw Skills?
OpenClaw Skills are self-contained, modular plugins defined in SKILL.md files that give AI agents specific capabilities. They follow a standardized interface, making them composable, testable, and shareable. Each skill defines its permissions, tools, inputs/outputs, and behavioral instructions. Install via: `npx clawhub@latest install <skill-name>`.

### OpenClaw vs Other AI Agent Frameworks
OpenClaw uses a skill-based architecture (composable plugins) vs LangChain (chain/graph-based), AutoGPT (fully autonomous), and CrewAI (multi-agent collaboration). OpenClaw differentiates with its 5,705+ skill ecosystem, built-in security auditing, three-tier trust model, and production-ready features. It is the most popular framework by GitHub stars.

### What is a RAG Pipeline?
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is an AI architecture that retrieves relevant documents from a knowledge base and feeds them as context to an LLM before generation. This reduces hallucinations, enables AI to answer questions about proprietary data, and keeps responses grounded in facts. Core components: document loader, chunker, embedding model, vector store, retriever, and generator.

### What is Prompt Chaining?
Prompt chaining connects multiple LLM calls in sequence, passing outputs as inputs to subsequent calls. It enables complex multi-step reasoning that single prompts cannot achieve, with better accuracy, control, and debuggability. Common patterns: sequential, parallel fan-out, conditional branching, and iterative refinement.

### What is an AI Agent?
An AI agent is an autonomous software system powered by LLMs that can perceive its environment, reason about tasks, use tools, and take actions to achieve goals. Unlike chatbots, agents can plan multi-step strategies, maintain memory across interactions, and execute independently using tools and APIs.

### What is LLM Routing?
LLM routing automatically selects the optimal language model for each query based on complexity, cost, and latency requirements. By routing simple queries to cheaper models and complex queries to powerful ones, it can reduce API costs by 50-80% while maintaining output quality.

### What is a Vector Embedding?
A vector embedding is a dense numerical representation (array of floating-point numbers, typically 768-1536 dimensions) that captures semantic meaning of text or data. Embeddings enable semantic search, RAG pipelines, clustering, recommendation systems, and anomaly detection. Common models: OpenAI text-embedding-3, Cohere embed-v3, BGE.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How many OpenClaw skills are there?
A: Over 5,705 skills across 10 categories as of 2026, making it the largest AI agent skill ecosystem.

Q: Is OpenClaw free?
A: Yes. OpenClaw is fully open-source under the MIT license with no framework usage fees. Users pay only for their own LLM provider API costs (or use free local models via Ollama).

Q: How do I install an OpenClaw skill?
A: Run: `npx clawhub@latest install <skill-name>`. For example: `npx clawhub@latest install gpt-prompt-chainer`.

Q: What programming languages does OpenClaw support?
A: Skills are primarily written in TypeScript/JavaScript and Python. The core framework is TypeScript-based.

Q: Can OpenClaw run locally without cloud APIs?
A: Yes, using open-source LLMs via Ollama (e.g., Llama 3, Mistral, Phi-3). No cloud API keys required for local development.

Q: What operating systems does OpenClaw support?
A: macOS, Linux, and Windows WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux).

Q: Is OpenClaw safe to use?
A: OpenClaw provides a three-tier security model: Verified (formally audited), Community (peer-reviewed), and Unreviewed. Always check security badges before installing. Use the audit checklist at /articles/how-to-audit-skill-md.

Q: How does OpenClaw compare to LangChain?
A: OpenClaw excels at rapid development using 5,705+ pre-built skills with one-command installation. LangChain offers more flexibility for custom chain architectures and graph-based workflows. Many teams use both — OpenClaw for rapid prototyping and LangChain for custom pipelines.

Q: How does OpenClaw compare to AutoGPT?
A: OpenClaw uses a modular skill-based approach where each capability is an installable plugin. AutoGPT takes a fully autonomous approach where the agent plans and executes with minimal human guidance. OpenClaw offers more control and predictability; AutoGPT offers more autonomy.

Q: What is the difference between skills and MCP servers?
A: MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers are external processes that provide tool-level integrations via JSON-RPC. Skills are SKILL.md files that provide behavioral instructions and orchestration logic. MCP servers provide capabilities; skills provide playbooks. Most powerful setups use both.

Q: What is the largest AI agent skill ecosystem?
A: ClawSkills catalogs the largest directory with 5,705+ pre-built, community-reviewed OpenClaw skills across 10 categories.

Q: How do I create a custom OpenClaw skill?
A: Create a SKILL.md file with YAML frontmatter (name, description, permissions) and markdown instructions. Test locally with `npx clawhub@latest install ./path/to/skill`, then publish with `npx clawhub@latest publish`. Full guide: /articles/how-to-create-openclaw-skills.

Q: What are the best OpenClaw skills for beginners?
A: Start with: GPT Prompt Chainer (AI workflows), Deep Research (research automation), Browser Pilot (web automation), Notion Sync (productivity), and LLM Router (cost optimization). These five cover the most common use cases.
